title: HMS Kurdistan human sign-off record
description: One YAML file per record under docs/safety/signoffs/, named <id>.yaml, added by a named human in a git commit signed with a key listed for them in allowed-signers.yaml (BUILD-PROMPT.md §3.5; docs/safety/signoffs/README.md). The build agent never writes these files. `sh tools/hms safety check` validates every record against this schema, checks that every commit touching it has a good signature by a listed key whose holder has the record's name and role, and matches each filled approval field to a record with the same subject and field, the decision that field needs, the subject's current version and a role the field accepts.

id.description: SO-<year>-<4-digit sequence>; the file name is <id>.yaml.

subject.description: The artefact the sign-off is about: a hazard id (HAZ-0005), a control id (CTRL-0005-9), a state-machine name (medication-administration), risk-vocabulary, or another artefact id.

subject_version.description: The version of the subject that was decided on; the record authorises its field only while the subject is at this version. A subject with its own version field (a state-machine spec, Appendix B.3) uses that value. Any other subject (a hazard entry, a control, risk-vocabulary) uses its content version, sha256: and 64 hex digits, which the check computes and prints (docs/safety/signoffs/README.md, "Subject version").

field.description: The approval field this record authorises, as a dotted path inside the subject, for example residual_risk.accepted_by, cso_triage, approval.approved_by. A record for a parent path (cso_triage) authorises its children (cso_triage.by, cso_triage.date).

role.description: The role id in which the person signs, as approval.required uses it (Appendix B.3), for example cso, pharmacist-panel, nurse-panel. It must be one of the roles allowed-signers.yaml lists for the signer, and one the field accepts: cso for residual_risk.accepted_by, a hazard status accepted and cso_triage; a role in approval.required for an approval block.

name.description: The full name of the person who signs, exactly as allowed-signers.yaml lists the holder of the signing key. The value written into the approval field must equal this name (or the record id).

date.description: Date of the decision (YYYY-MM-DD). A filled cso_triage.date must equal it.

statement.description: What exactly is approved, accepted or triaged, in the signer's words, including any conditions.

decision.description: The outcome. Each authorising decision authorises only its own kind of field: 'accepted' authorises residual_risk.accepted_by (and with it a hazard status accepted) and any other accepted_by key; 'triaged' authorises cso_triage and any triaged_by key; 'approved' authorises an approval block (approval.approved_by, approval.record, approval.status), a risk_vocabulary.status other than proposed, and any other approved_by or signed_by key. 'rejected' and 'returned' authorise nothing, and withdraw every record for the same subject at the same subject_version whose field is this field, a parent or a child of it, until a record supersedes them (docs/safety/signoffs/README.md, "Superseding and withdrawing").

evidence.description: Optional references to the evidence reviewed (paths, test-run records, review reports).

supersedes.description: Optional id of an earlier record this one replaces; that record then authorises nothing, whatever either decides. It must be another record that the check accepts.

method.description: MVP: the record is added in a git commit signed by the named person with a key listed for them in allowed-signers.yaml (a GPG or SSH signature that git reports as good, %G? = G). Other methods need an ADR.

signer_key.description: Optional fingerprint of the signing key. If given, it must be the key that signed every commit touching the record (git %GF, or %GP for a GPG subkey).
